summary: John's 4th-great-grandfather; Plymouth farmer, son of Samuel and Martha (Lamoreaux) Pringle, who married into the Palatine German Croup family.
bio:
James Pringle was born about 1799 in Pennsylvania (1850 census: 51, farmer, real estate $500, b. PA); the tree shows 1798-?, and a FamilySearch profile's '1799-1909' death is impossible (probably a merge). He was a son of Samuel Pringle and Martha Lamoreaux (Harvey Book pp.370-371, via his son Noah). He married Elizabeth Croup, daughter of Frederick Croup and Mary Young of Hunlock's Creek/Nanticoke. In 1850 the household in Plymouth Twp (dwelling 944/family 964, 14 Sep 1850) was James 51, Elizabeth 48, Alby 27, Noah 16, Andrew 14, Leva Ann 11 and Edwin 9; neighbours were Jenkins Jones (36, miner, Wales; dwelling 943) and Thomas Gould (39, farmer, $2,500; dwelling 945), with his probable sister-in-law the widow Hulda Pringle at dwelling 942. FamilySearch gives a second wife, Mary Steele (d. 15 Jul 1876), and burial in Scott Cemetery, Huntington Mills. He is not the runaway apprentice 'James Pringle', about 14, advertised by Isaac Smith of Exeter Twp on 9 Apr 1836, nor his uncle James Pringle who married Phebe Lamoreux in 1785.

James was still farming in Plymouth in August 1860, aged 61, with real estate valued at $1,200 (more than double the $500 of 1850); his wife Elizabeth (57) and youngest son Edwin (18) were at home, together with a seven-year-old, Mary Williams, perhaps a grandchild or a bound girl, and his son Andrew had set up house next door ([R4-S1]). By 29 July 1870 James, 71, was living in Andrew's household and Elizabeth was no longer listed, so she had probably died between 1860 and 1870 ([R4-S2]). James therefore died after July 1870, not in 1909 as the FamilySearch profile says.

The FamilySearch profile (KP7T-1HK) is a merge of two different men. It attaches the 1867 Toronto marriage of Thomas Murray Pringle, aged 28, born in Scotland, son of 'James & Mary Pringle' ([R4-S3]), and gives this James children born at Ruthven, Angus, Scotland, in 1834 and 1839. That Scottish James and his wife Mary are evidently the source of the 'second wife Mary' on the profile, which has been identified with Mary Steele (1808-1876). But FamilySearch's own Mary Steele profile shows her as the wife of John Linskill (d. 1865), mother of six Linskill children born in Lehman Twp 1833-48, living as 'Mary Linchkill' in 1860, and buried as Mary Steele Linskill at Huntsville, Jackson Twp ([R4-S4]). No record of a marriage between Johnny's James and Mary (Steele) Linskill was found; the 'second marriage' should be treated as an error unless a record turns up. (Mary Steele was a daughter of Peter Steele and Charity Lamoreaux, so she was James's first cousin, which may also have helped the confusion.)

researchLog.note: Imported from the project handoff (research rounds 1–3, Oct 2026).
Birth in the Ancestry tree: 1798; research: ABT 1799.

Resolved: Confirm second marriage to Mary Steele. → Not confirmed and probably false: the FamilySearch profile merges a Scottish James Pringle (wife Mary; son Thomas Murray Pringle b. Scotland, m. Toronto 1867), and Mary Steele was the widow of John Linskill, buried under that name.
Resolved: Death date and place (FS '1909' impossible). → Partly: alive at 71 on 29 Jul 1870 in son Andrew's household in Plymouth Twp; death after that date (not found).

Round 4 searched without result: PAGenWeb Luzerne Shupp Cemetery transcription (Larksville): no Pringle; PAGenWeb Huntington Twp cemetery pages: no Scott Cemetery transcription online; Web search 'Scott Cemetery' 'Huntington Mills' Pringle: no relevant result

Round 4: 1860 and 1870 censuses show James farming next to son Andrew (1860) and living with him at 71 (1870); FamilySearch 'second wife Mary Steele' traced to a merge with a Scottish James & Mary Pringle of Toronto.
